incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 - GPU pool us-west-2-prod-gpu-pool — multiple thermal spikes + VRAM OOMs detected, autoscaler started draining nodes. Pager routed to #eng-oncall. Alerts: GPUHighTemp, GPUVramOOM, GPUEccRate. Link: https://metrics.redwood.example/alerts/1987654321

Ben: I'm on it. Acknowledging pager and jumping in. Any initial customer impact flags?

incident-bot: Noted: ~2% error rate increase for hosted API routes using gptx-large; several dedicated customers report intermittent request timeouts. See incident stream: https://incidents.redwood.example/1987654321

Carla: Looking at runtime logs. I see repeated kernels being reloaded and multiple `OOMKilled` events on pod gpu-srv-12. Also thermal throttling at the kernel level: `gpu_temp=92C` spikes followed by node drain.

Alice: FYI: autoscaler drained 3 nodes in the pool in the last 8m. Pod redistribution caused momentary queueing. We're seeing tail latencies spike to ~1.2s for generation calls. Not full outage but customer-facing degradation.

Dave: I'm going to open capacity and fail traffic to other regions for sensitive routes. Posting a quick routing change to redirect dedicated customers with SLO>99.9 to us-east for next 30m.

Emily: Support: I already messaged the three dedicated accounts affected; two reported retries, one reported sustained latency. Will post an update to customers after we have mitigation plan.

Frank: Observability notes — alert noise is the problem here. The thermal alert is firing on instantaneous max temp; we should switch to a 3m rolling average to avoid flapping. Also ECC alerts are noisy: a few single-bit ECC increments shouldn't page. Propose: add a `for: 5m` to GPUEccRate and add threshold that triggers on rate > 0.5 errors/min aggregated per node.

Ben: Agreed. For immediate triage, can we mute the duplicate GPUEccRate pages (we still want post-incident telemetry)? Frank, can you add a silence and add a dashboard snapshot?

Frank: Adding silence now (temporary). Command I ran:
```
amtool silence add --match 'alertname=GPUEccRate' --duration=30m --comment 'silence noisy ECC pages during thermal incident 1987654321'
```
Dashboard snapshot: https://dashboards.redwood.example/d/thermal/1987654321-snapshot

Carla: As a quick mitigation, I scaled down low-priority batch jobs on the pool and bumped the thermal governor to be slightly more conservative on affected nodes. Also pinned some hot models to lower sequence lengths.

Ben: Thanks. Also we need to avoid blind lowering of thresholds. We should distinguish between nodes with known cooling issues (open ticket with infra) vs fleet-wide rule changes.

Greg: Post-incident action plan (short):
- Triage and get nodes repaired (infra ticket) - Dave + Carla
- Add 3m rolling average for GPUHighTemp alert and move threshold to 88C for non-critical pools - Frank + Alice
- Add `for: 5m` to GPUEccRate and set rate-based threshold - Frank
- Create a VRAM OOM debouncing mechanism: fire only if >3 pods OOM on same node in 10m - Carla + Alice
- Update alert runbook and dashboard panels: new thermals view, ECC rate histogram - Alice + Frank
- Customer comms: status note and follow-up - Emily
- Postmortem and follow-up JIRA: INF-987 - Greg

Alice: I'll create the PR for alertmanager rules and dashboards. Expected diff snippet for GPU temp rule:
```
- alert: GPUHighTemp
- expr: max_over_time(gpu_temp{pool="prod-gpu"}[1m]) > 85
+ alert: GPUHighTemp
+ expr: max_over_time(gpu_temp{pool="prod-gpu"}[3m]) > 88
+ for: 5m
```
Planning to put this behind a feature flag for specific pools first.

Frank: For ECC we should also include debounce: `increase(gpu_ecc_errors_total[5m]) / 5 > 0.5` so short spikes don't page. I'll author that rule and add a test in the alerting repo.

Dave: Infra ticket created: INFRA-4521 — suspected cooling shroud partial failure on rack r-usw2-14. Tagging hw-team. I've also requested an on-site replacement for the affected fans.

Emily: Drafting customer-facing update: short note that some dedicated customers in us-west experienced elevated latencies due to GPUs being drained for thermal mitigation; we routed traffic and reduced impact. ETA for full recovery TBD; will update in 30m.

Carla: After scaling batch and changing pins, latency is improving. Tail p95 back to ~300ms for most routes. No new OOMs in the last 10m.

Ben: Great. Let's keep the silence periods as temporary. Do not disable alerts permanently. Post-incident we implement the tuned rules and run for 48-72h with lower-severity paging and higher retention for ECC events.

Greg: Assigning owners: Frank (alert rule changes + dashboard PR), Alice (runbook + VRAM OOM debounce), Carla (node repairs + model pinning playbook), Dave (hardware replacement), Emily (customer comms), Ben (incident commander until handoff). I'll collect notes and schedule the postmortem.

Ben: Handoff in 30m to on-call night shift. If anything pages in the meantime ping me @Ben. Otherwise I'll update ops channel at 1987654388 with final status. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident 1987654321 updated: mitigations applied, silences added, hardware ticket INFRA-4521 created. Current status: partial degraded -> recoverable.

Ben: Closing loop for now — monitoring closely.
